events.title: 美國以安全考量為由退出卡達U17世界盃
events.special_reason: 國家隊因安全考量退出國際賽事
events.why_matters: 國際足壇國家隊因安全疑慮退出世界級大賽具備重大影響力。
events.summary: 美國足球協會考量武裝衝突風險，宣佈退出在卡達舉行的U17世界盃。此決定基於美國國務院對卡達發布的第三級旅遊警示，警告葉門青年運動組織攻擊鄰近國家機場等威脅，並指出區域敵對情勢有迅速升級的潛力。原定於11月19日至12月13日進行的賽事中，美國原本要在小組賽對陣蒙特內哥羅、智利與阿爾及利亞。
events.note: 綜合BBC、ESPN與AP報導美國退出U17世界盃及安全考量。
events.context:
【BBC Sport】Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The USA reached the last 32 of last year's Under-17 World Cup, the first of five successive editions to be held annually in Qatar The USA have withdrawn from the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar because of the risk of armed conflict. In a letter sent to players and seen by news agency Reuters, US Soccer said it made the decision "in light of current circumstances". It cited advice from the US Department of State, which issued a level three travel advisory , external for Qatar last month. That came a day after Yemen's Houthi movement carried out a deadly attack on an airport in neighbouring Saudi Arabia, while air strikes have continued on Saudi Arabia and Yemen. The 48-team tournament runs from 19 November to 13 December, and the USA were due to play group games against Montenegro, Chile and Algeria. The US travel advisory mentioned Houthi attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure, and warned that hostilities "have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area". The update told Americans to reconsider travel to Qatar because of "risk of armed conflict". "The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority," US Soccer said in the letter. It said it would notify the players' clubs and asked players not to comment publicly until their withdrawal has been announced by tournament organisers Fifa. The 2027 Asian Cup - Asia's version of the European Championships - was due to take place in Saudi Arabia from 7 January to 5 February, but has been postponed by almost a year because of the conflict. The wife of England striker Ollie Watkins, who plays in the Saudi Pro League, has taken their children back to the UK until the situation "calms down".
